The issue seems to be in the `org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.tar.TarArchiveInputStream.parsePaxHeaders` method. The method is responsible for parsing PAX headers from an input stream. The bug report mentions that the method fails with a NegativeArraySizeException when there is an empty line at the end of the headers.

Looking at the code snippet of the `parsePaxHeaders` method, the issue likely occurs in the inner loop that reads the header length and processes the header data. The loop calculates the length of the header entry, and if a newline character is encountered instead of a digit, it may result in a negative length value, leading to the NegativeArraySizeException when allocating an array for the header content.

To address this issue, a check should be added to ensure that the character read is a digit before updating the length calculation. This check will prevent negative lengths from being calculated and avoid the NegativeArraySizeException.

Next, I'll suggest the method that needs to be fixed.

The `org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.tar.TarArchiveInputStream.parsePaxHeaders` method documentation does not provide specific details on handling edge cases like empty lines at the end of the headers. To prevent the NegativeArraySizeException, a validation should be added to ensure proper handling of characters that are not digits during length calculations.

The method that needs to be fixed is:
`org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.tar.TarArchiveInputStream.parsePaxHeaders(java.io.InputStream)`

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
